where: Section 1 (repeated in the figure note, Worked example 1, Exam traps and Quiz Q2)
problem: The text says each concatenated part 'spends 7 bytes on a user data header'. The concatenation header is 6 bytes (octets): 1 length byte + 1 IEI + 1 IE length + 3 data bytes (reference, total parts, sequence). Six octets are 48 bits, which after 7-bit packing occupy 7 characters (septets) of the 160. So the loss is 7 characters, not 7 bytes. A student will write 'the UDH is 7 bytes' in the exam, which is wrong.
fix: Say: the user data header is 6 bytes, and after 7-bit packing it costs 7 of the 160 characters, leaving 153 characters of payload per part (160 − 7 = 153). In the figure note write '6-byte header takes 7 chars', not '7-bit GSM header'.

problem: The text says to catch ActivityNotFoundException if no app matches, but just before it says to wrap the intent in Intent.createChooser. When the intent is launched through createChooser, the chooser activity itself handles the no-match case and shows its own message; ActivityNotFoundException is thrown when you start an implicit intent directly with no chooser.
fix: Say: with createChooser the chooser shows its own 'no apps' message; the try/catch for ActivityNotFoundException is needed when you start ACTION_SENDTO (or any implicit intent) directly without a chooser.

problem: The list of extras mixes two intents. EXTRA_EMAIL is not a reliable way to set recipients for ACTION_SENDTO; with ACTION_SENDTO the address belongs in the mailto: URI, and some mail apps ignore EXTRA_EMAIL there. A student may build a SENDTO intent with EXTRA_EMAIL and find the To: field empty.
fix: Say: for ACTION_SENDTO put the address in the URI, e.g. Uri.parse("mailto:someone@example.com"); EXTRA_EMAIL is used when you attach recipients to ACTION_SEND/ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE.

problem: SmsManager.getDefault() is deprecated from Android 12 (API 31). Students targeting recent SDKs will see a deprecation warning and, on multi-SIM phones, cannot choose the SIM.
fix: Keep getDefault() for older APIs but add: on API 31 and later use context.getSystemService(SmsManager.class), which also supports per-SIM managers.
